News.title: Dior executive, 57, killed in horror car crash with film producer boyfriend as tributes paid to ‘exceptional woman’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

‘LOST A FRIEND’ Dior executive, 57, killed in horror car crash with film producer boyfriend as tributes paid to ‘exceptional woman’

A DIOR exec and her film producer boyfriend have been killed in a horrific car crash in France.

Tributes have poured in for Mathilde Favier, 57, who has been described as an “exceptional woman” by the fashion dynasty.



The pair reportedly collided with a “heavy goods vehicle” while trying to pass another car.

Mathilde served as director of public relations at Christian Dior Couture.



Dior released a statement on Tuesday morning, calling her an “exceptional woman”.

A statement read: “Dior is deeply saddened to announce the accidental death of Mathilde Favier.



“In her role as Director of Public Relations, Mathilde Favier made an incredible contribution to the reputation of Christian Dior Couture through her commitment and elegance.

“She was an exceptional woman whose communicative joy, talent, and loyalty were exemplary.”

Dior CEO Delphine Arnault mourned the loss of a “loyal friend” in a touching message.

She wrote: “Mathilde loved life with a passion. With the passing of Mathilde, Dior is losing an incredible professional, and I have lost a loyal friend.



“Her optimism and courage commanded admiration. We will sorely miss her smile and her talent.

“I feel deeply saddened today; my thoughts are very much with her children, her mother, her sisters, her family, her many friends and her team she loved so much.”

Mathilde shared two children – Helen, 27, and Carlo, 25 – with her first husband Robert Agostinelli.

Finance magnate Agostinelli is a self-made billionaire who is the chairman and co-founder of private equity firm Rhône Group.

News.title: Man, 18, arrested after girl, 2, hit with e-bike and airlifted to hospital with serious injuries
News.content:
TOT HORROR Man, 18, arrested after girl, 2, hit with e-bike and airlifted to hospital with serious injuries

AN 18-year-old man has been arrested after a toddler was seriously injured after being hit by an e-bike.

The two-year-old girl was airlifted to hospital from the scene at Clacton, Essex, at around 9pm on Thursday.

Cops scrambled to the incident but the rider failed to stop and officers launched an investigation to trace him.

A man from Clacton has now been arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by dangerous driving and released on bail.





Police confirmed that the tot sustained seriously injuries and remains in hospital.

Several witnesses were stopped at the scene and now cops are pursuing several lines of enquiry and appealing for information from the public.

A spokesperon for Essex Police said: “Our officers have arrested a teenager in connection with a serious collision in Clacton.

“We were called to reports of a collision involving an electric bike and a two-year-old pedestrian in Pathfields Road at about 9pm.

“The child sustained serious injuries and was taken to hospital by air ambulance where she remains.

“The rider failed to stop at the scene and our officers quickly launched an investigation to locate them.

“Now, an 18-year-old man from Clacton has been arrested in suspicion of causing serious injury by dangerous driving. He has been bailed until 10 November while our enquiries continue.”

They added: “You can still contact us if you have any information, CCTV, dash cam or other footage in relation to this incident and have not already spoken to our officers.



“Please quote 1436 of 13 August.

“You can let us know by submitting a report on our website or by using our online Live Chat service which is available 24 hours-a-day, seven days-a-week.

“If you would like to make an anonymous report you can contact independent charity Crimestoppers, by visiting their website or by calling 0800 555 111.”

News.title: I was raped at knifepoint by intruder while my toddler slept – monster explained why in chilling two-word confession
News.content:
READING peacefully in bed after an exhausting day visiting her husband in hospital, a 32-year-old mother had no idea of the monster lurking in the shadows of her Surrey home.

In a heartbeat, her world was shattered when the horrifying silhouette of 28-year-old Lee Hill appeared in the darkness outside her bedroom.



Armed with a pen-knife, the twisted intruder slashed her, threatened to kill her, and vowed to murder her two-year-old daughter sleeping defencelessly in the room next door.

For four agonising hours, the terrified mum was tortured and repeatedly raped in a nightmare ordeal – that Hill later chillingly admitted was “for fun”.

Just hours after surviving her attack, the selfless mum put on a brave face to throw a birthday party for her daughter.



Astonishingly, Hill had been released from prison just five months earlier after serving a nine-year sentence for another brutal attack.

In June 1993, he had broken into a woman’s home through a study window – using a metal lawn edge trimmer stolen from her garden shed to saw through the lock – before punching her in the face and raping her on her living room sofa for over an hour.

When Hill was finally brought to justice in 2000 he was handed three life sentences with a 25-year minimum term.

Sentencing Judge Valerie Pearlman warned he was “very dangerous,” had “great potential for harm to women,” and was “likely to commit similar offences in the future”.

Detective Sergeant Stephen Farley, who caught the beast, similarly branded him a “danger to women” for many years to come.



Hill, from Walton-on-Thames, was placed on the sex offenders’ register and police licence for life.

And bravely trying to regain her life, his victim became a counsellor working with victims of crime.

Yet the nightmare did not end there.

First eligible for parole in 2012, Hill met his victim behind bars in 2014 during a restorative justice session.

There, the cold-blooded rapist – who had just had a failed suicide attempt days previously – made a chilling confession: he had planned to break in and attack someone purely for his own enjoyment.



His victim bravely told The Sun: “He didn’t commit a crime because he had to feed his children or he had a heroin addiction – he does this for fun.”

Maintaining her right to anonymity, the woman added: “This is his recreation.

“It’s sick and it’s very, very dangerous… sex offenders like him can’t be rehabilitated, let’s be frank.”



But she still found the ability to forgive her attacker – causing him to break down in tears.

Determined to protect others, the brave mother spent years campaigning alongside government ministers and the parole board to improve how the justice system treats victims and to keep her attacker behind bars.

She repeatedly warned authorities that Hill was an “extreme danger” who would strike again.

Her pleas were ignored.

In June 2024, the parole board declared Hill, now 51, safe to be managed in the community and set him free.



Now, less than two years after his controversial release, the monster has been hauled back behind bars.

And his victim – already dealing with the trauma of his release – has been kept in the dark over why he has once again been caged.

Probation officers put Hill back in prison last week, but are refusing to tell the mum-of-two why he was recalled.

Efforts by The Sun to establish why he has been recalled have also been resisted by the Ministry of Justice.

“I think it’s cruel that they won’t tell me,” she said.



“They put the victims last, as ever.”

A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said: “Offenders released on license are subject to strict conditions, and we do not hesitate to recall them to prison if they break the rules and pose a risk to the public.”

News.title: Glam Scots influencer caught smuggling £150k of dope from Thailand poses at music festival months after being jailed
News.content:
A GLAM social media influencer who was caught smuggling £150,000

worth of cannabis has been pictured partying at a music festival –

weeks after being sentenced to 16 months in jail.

Ellie Crampsie, 23, posted pictures and videos from the Coloursfest

dance event in Braehead, near Glasgow, on her Instagram and TikTok

accounts



In one caption she boasts ‘they can never keep a bad b***h down’.

In another clip shared online she struts towards the camera wearing

knee-high boots, hotpants and dark glasses with the phrase: “When I’m

baddest bitch he’ll ever meet.”



A pal replied: “He he he, love you sexy”, while another follower

added: “You know it”.

The mobile phone footage was filmed over the weekend.

On April 24 this year Crampsie was handed down a 16-month jail term.

But in another example of soft-touch justice she’s back living the

high life – despite a high-profile National Crime Agency campaign

warning about the consequences of being a drugs mule.



It’s one of a stream of videos Crampise has posted after being

released early under a curfew that includes wearing a tag.

In another video she is seen posing with a pal who plants a kiss on

her cheek as they make sultry poses in front of the camera.

Crampsie wrote: “All you need in life is your girlies.”

She is also seen posing in pink gym gear as she shows off her figure

with a caption pledging: “2006 is the year for bettering yourself

queens.”

We told how a sheriff earlier branded Crampsie “reckless” and “naive”

to traffick 17 kilos of hash in her luggage on her return from a

holiday in Thailand.



The brazen brows firm founder continued to flaunt flash jaunts to

Morocco and Spain to online followers after she was arrested at

Edinburgh Airport in April last year.

But she was stony-faced and stared at her family at being told in

court she would be sent down.

Sheriff Graeme Watson accepted Crampsie had possibly been “taken

advantage of” after hearing claims she had been acting under the

influence of a former unnamed boyfriend.

But he said there was no alternative to jail.

Lawyer Michael Poggi told Edinburgh Sheriff Court: “A much older

person had a controlling position over my client.”



Crampsie, of Broomhouse, Glasgow, earlier admitted being concerned in

the supply of drugs.

She is one of many smugglers caught in recent months for bringing dope

to the UK from the South East Asian Country.

We told how Britain’s answer to the FBI has ramped up warnings over

The National Crime Agency’s new social media campaign hammers home the risks involved in becoming a courier with the prospect of huge fines

Beki Wright, Borders Threat Lead at the NCA, said: “Criminal gangs are

targeting social media users with the promise of a free holiday and

easy money.”



A Scottish Prison Service spokesperson said: “We do not comment on individuals.

“We only release those in our care on a Home Detention Curfew after a

News.title: Paralysed campaigner, 44, who ran marathon in ‘bionic’ suit died in microlight crash while filming Apple TV series
News.content:
TRAGIC SMASH Paralysed campaigner, 44, who ran marathon in ‘bionic’ suit died in microlight crash while filming Apple TV series

A PARALYSED campaigner who became the first person to complete a marathon in a “bionic” suit died in a microlight crash while filming for an Apple TV series, an inquest heard.

Claire Lomas, who was paralysed from the chest down after a horse-riding accident, “veered off the runway” and hit a large rock while landing the aircraft on July 15, 2024.



The 44-year-old suffered multiple severe traumatic injuries during the horror in Jordan and died more than five weeks later in hospital.

An inquest heard Claire was in the Middle East filming for a series for Apple’s VR headset.



Lina Zilinskaite, who is a senior producer for Atlantic Productions, said: “Each episode follows a different athlete performing some sort of challenge or feat.

“(It was) always controlled risk. Individuals were doing this as a big hobby or profession in some instances. We are not plucking people off the street to do it.”

Lina said Claire was “delighted” to be selected and was “very enthusiastic and keen and excited about the opportunity”.

Claire got a licence to fly a microlight, which is a small aircraft, a few years before the tragedy, the court heard.



The production company reportedly knew she needed help getting in and out of the specially adapted aircraft because she was paraplegic.

Senior coroner for Rutland and North Leicestershire, Louise Pinder, said the wind strength was “light and from the left which is considered normal” on the day of the crash.

She said it would have been preferable to have a smaller camera on the microlight, but it did not exceed the weight limit for take-off.

The inquest heard the flight was cancelled the day before because of strong winds.

On the day of the horror, Claire flew in the air for about 15 minutes before attempting to land.



But she tragically “hit a large rock” and was taken by a standby ambulance to hospital in a critical condition.

Lina said: “She veered off the runway then I just heard this noise.”

Mum Claire was said to be “excited” to come home with her family after spending weeks in hospital but was struck down with an infection and deteriorated quickly, the inquest heard.

She tragically passed away on August 22, 2024.

Former chiropractor Claire broke her neck, back and ribs and punctured a lung when her horse threw her off as she took part in the Osberton Horse Trials in Nottinghamshire.



She completed the London Marathon in 17 days in 2012 using a “bionic” suit – raising thousands of pounds for the Spinal Research charity.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Claire was also a motivational speaker, a qualified pilot and was made an MBE in 2017.

The inquest continues.

News.title: Wife’s chilling prediction before stalker husband stabbed her and her mum to death as police ignored her pleas for help
News.content:
TERRIFIED for her life, Raneem Oudeh pleaded with the police for the fourth time in two hours to help after her abusive ex husband threatened to kill her.

The 22 year-old was told by officers to go back to her mother’s home, where evil Janbaz Tarin, 21, was waiting for them in a bush with a 13-inch knife.



Raneem and her 49-year-old mum Khaola Saleem were brutally stabbed to death by Tarin, who fled the scene and led police on a three-day manhunt.

The double murder, which took place in Solihull in 2018 and is featured on ITV’s Murder UK series, shocked the nation and ripped apart their family.



Nour Norris – Khaola’s sister and Raneem’s aunt – said in the documentary how a shaken Raneem had told her she feared her abusive ex-husband would take her life.

Nour said: “She [Raneem] said to me, ‘auntie I think he’s going to kill me.’



“And I said ‘we have the authority. We have the police. You need to report all of this.’

“She said ‘I did’. She said ‘they are not going to do anything.They always listen to what he says, not to me. Because he’s very good at manipulating them.’”



Raneem was just 19 when she met Tarin at Solihull College, with her family coming to the UK to seek a safe haven after fleeing war-torn Syria.

Describing her niece as being “very pretty” and having a “beautiful character”, Nour said: “Raneem when she came she loved it.

“She had a great voice and she wanted to be a singer one day. She had all the hopes in the world when she came to the UK.

“She thought she was coming somewhere safe due to the war in Syria.

“She was happy to just study and she didn’t want anything else really. I don’t think she really wanted a man in her life.”



However, on their first meeting, controlling Tarin told Raneem “you’ll be mine” and started calling her obsessively and trying to force her into a relationship.

Nour said: “He had a very strong character and was ‘I’m the man here’, and everyone in some ways thought he was great.

“He’d spend a lot of money on everybody. He’d buy her lunch for her sake and was very much a man of control.”

The hounding briefly stopped when Raneem married another man, but the relationship ended a few days before giving birth to their son.

Shortly after, in June 2016, Tarin came back into Raneem’s life and started threatening her by saying he would hurt her family unless she married him.



Nour said: “I know Raneen, she is quite soft so he can persuade her at some point.”

She added: “I think she was trying to be strong and clever by going along with his plan but didn’t know what she was going along with.”

In September 2016, Raneem and Tarin had an islamic marriage, which is not legally recognised in the UK, with her being told that if she ever left him he would kill her and her family.



Her aunt said Tarin, who worked as a cashier at his dad’s convenience store, was physically and mentally abusive towards his new wife, and Raneem became distant from her family.

Nour explained: “She kept disappearing and not wanting anyone to come down to her house.

“She tried her best to show us that she was fine.

“She didn’t want it to end because she knows if he ends it, it’s the end of her life.

“We knew it was very bad, but we didn’t know how bad it was.”



Things took a turn for the worse in 2017 when Tarin went on a visit to his native Afghanistan, and it was then that Raneem discovered her husband had a pregnant wife and two children there.

Desperate to break free of the marriage and fearing for her life, Raneem told him she was leaving in 2018 and told the police she felt like she was in danger.

However, Tarin ramped up his reign of terror and harassment, one time sleeping for 12 consecutive days in a car outside her mum’s home.



At her mother Khaola’s suggestion, Raneem took out a non-molestation order against Tarin, meaning he couldn’t come near her or contact her directly, and she moved in with her for safety.

On August 26, 2018, the pair had spent the day shopping and visiting family together, and went to Rotana Sheesha bar in Birmingham in the evening.

Unbeknown to them, Tarin had been stalking their every move in a white van borrowed from work, and breached his non-molestation order to confront them inside in a jealous tirade.



Chilling CCTV footage showed Tarin attacking mum-of-six Khaola, slapping her, before grabbing Raneem’s phone and threatening to kill her making a throat-splitting gesture.

The violent behaviour was done in front of a crowd of customers – before Tarin was thrown out.

Terrified, Raneem called the police at 10.30pm and she and Khaola waited in the cold for half an hour before retreating to their car.

During this time, Tarin went to his family’s shop to arm himself with a weapon – a sharp 13-inch kitchen knife used to cut meat.



Nour said: “There was no police chasing him. He was on the loose. He was doing whatever he wanted to do.

“He wanted to take her life because he didn’t love her. He thought she was one of his things. “He owned her. She can’t go for someone else. She can’t be free.”

At midnight, police called Raneem back and told them to go home and lock their doors and call them if he came back.

Little did they know that Tarin was lying in wait for them outside.



Raneem called the police again as she crossed the lawn to her front door – and screamed hysterically as Tarin jumped out from the bushes and began a frenzied attack.

As Khaola stepped in to protect her daughter, she was also stabbed to death.

Shockingly the attack was witnessed by Raneem’s step-sister, Khaola’s youngest daughter, who was just 15 at the time.



After a three day manhunt, Tarin was found hiding in the store room of a Birmingham corner shop.

In December 2018 he was sentenced to life with a minimum tariff of 32 years.

An inquest into their deaths found 33 police officers had “materially contributed” to their death.

Misconduct notices were served to nine West Midland police officers and the police watchdog described the situation as “profoundly disturbing”.

Nour says lessons need to be learned.



She said: “We need to protect women by allowing their voices to be heard. By making a better system.

“Those vulnerable women we need to give them wings. We need to make them stronger, not weaker.”

Now a trained counsellor Nour has helped raise Raneem’s son along with his dad, and supports other families bereaved by murder.

Speaking of her tragic family loss, she said she gets some comfort knowing Raneem and Khaola are at peace together.

She shared: “I know my sister wouldn’t survive it if Raneem went and she didn’t.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Knowing they are both together and they are happier together, than one without the other.”

News.title: Body of man, 41, found in city centre multi-storey car park as cops probe ‘unexplained’ death
News.content:
GRIM FIND Body of man, 41, found in city centre multi-storey car park as cops probe ‘unexplained’ death

COPS have launched a probe after a man was tragically discovered dead in a city centre car park.

Officers found the body of the 41-year-old on the ground floor of the multi-storey in Truro, Cornwall, yesterday.



The grim discovery was made after the alarm was raised at Moorfield Car Park in Calenick Street.

A 41-year-old man, from the local area, was sadly found dead on the ground floor of the car park.



An investigation was quickly launched following his “unexplained” death, Devon and Cornwall Police confirmed.

His next of kin have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers while enquiries remain ongoing, the force added.

A police cordon is currently in place around the ground floor while forensic examinations and searches are carried out.

Eyewitnesses first reported seeing police cars descend upon the car park at around 3pm.

It was later confirmed by cops that paramedics were also in attendance.

Several police vehicles and forensic officers remained at the scene until 6pm yesterday, with the car park completely cordoned off.



Customers were forced to wait as officers returned vehicles to them.

CCTV footage is currently being reviewed to establish the man’s final movements before he died.

The force are also appealing for anyone who may have information to come forward.

Witnesses who saw anything suspicious between last Friday afternoon and 10.45am yesterday are being urged to get in touch.

Detective Inspector Jon Bray said: “Our enquiries are at an early stage as we work to establish the circumstances surrounding this man’s death.



“We are appealing to anyone who may have information or witnessed anything suspicious in the area between the afternoon of Friday 14 August and 10.45am on Monday 17 August.

“There will be an ongoing police presence in the area while enquiries continue and anyone with concerns is encouraged to speak with officers at the scene.

“The inside ground floor car parking area will remain closed today while detectives and specialist teams carry out their investigations.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We would like to thank the public for their patience and understanding around the ongoing police presence.

“Anyone requiring access to a vehicle within the cordoned area should speak to officers at the scene who will assist them.”

News.title: Architect ‘threatened to kill beautician & her daughter in chilling abuse spat after he botched plans for her clinic’
News.content:
HATE WAR Architect ‘threatened to kill beautician & her daughter in chilling abuse spat after he botched plans for her clinic’

AN ARCHITECT threatened to kill a beautician and her daughter after he botched plans for her clinic, a tribunal heard.

Joan Beltri allegedly launched the “campaign of harassment, abuse and threats” towards Carolina Sampietro and her oral surgeon husband Dr James Escoda-Francoli.



A tribunal heard Beltri had been hired to work on the clinic they were building in Winchester, Hampshire, but the relationship soured after a number of blunders.

The architect cut through a gas pipe while doing work he was unqualified for and also failed to secure permission from the council to renovate the Grade II-listed building.



During the hate campaign, Beltri was said to have bombarded Carolina and her husband with emails and voicemails.

One said: “said: “I will kill them all. It’s what I will do. Their parents, their family, and their children.”

Beltri also allegedly accused Carolina of sleeping with other men said: “If I saw you in the street, I would spit in your face”.

He has now been struck off by the Architects Registration Board (ARB) following the tribunal.

The panel heard Beltri started working for the couple in August 2024 after they purchased the building and planned to turn it into an aesthetic clinic.

But there were rows between the architect and his clients, which were often centred around which work should be subcontracted and which work he should do himself.



The couple ended Beltri’s contract in November 2024 and also reported him to the Architects Registration Board (ARB).

He then became increasingly abusive towards Carolina and Dr Escoda-Francoli.

Beltri left a voicemail saying “I have never come across such a son of a b***h as you” and branded them a “bunch of motherf*****s”.



It was heard he also threatened the couple’s daughter while speaking to ARB officials.

Beltri told the tribunal: “I do not apologise for the communications because I maintain that I did not use abusive or threatening language.

“I do not accept the characterisation of my conduct as harassment, abuse or threats.”

In their findings, the panel said the communications were “deeply distressing”.

It added: “The Committee is satisfied that it is appropriate to describe [Mr Beltri]’s actions as a campaign of harassment, abuse and threats from April until August 2025, when the ARB instructed solicitors to write to [Mr Beltri].”



Speaking after the tribunal, Carolina said the experience had been a “nightmare”.

She continued: “He was sending me hundreds of emails every day. He still calls me today. I blocked him everywhere, but you can see he is still sending me things.

“He tried to get on to my social accounts. I receive emails like someone tried to enter your account. My Facebook account was blocked because there were so many attempts to enter my account.

“He is obsessed with all of this, but with me particularly. He doesn’t go after my husband usually. He is more abusive with me.

“I reported him to the police and at the moment he is living in Spain so that is better.”

News.title: British couple on honeymoon killed in helicopter crash on Greek island
News.content:
A young British couple and their pilot were killed in a helicopter crash on the Greek island of Sifnos on Monday, Greek police have said.

They have been named as newlyweds Alexander Cromie and Marie Ebert, who were in Greece on their honeymoon.

The private helicopter crashed just metres from a landing pad, killing the pair and their pilot, a Greek national.

The couple are said to have taken the helicopter from the village of Markopoulo near Athens to the popular holiday island, Kathimerini reported.

Greece's aviation safety authority told the BBC it was investigating the crash and that its investigators were heading to the scene on Tuesday to gather evidence and speak to witnesses.

News.title: Serco employee charged with misconduct over sharing asylum seeker addresses in Thetford
News.content:
An employee of a company that provides accommodation for asylum seekers has been charged with misconduct in public office over sharing the properties' addresses.

Houses in St John's Way, Bracken Road, Clover Way, Elm Road and Chester Way in Thetford, Norfolk, were targeted by crowds over three nights earlier this month.

James Jobson, 62, from Highlow Road, Costessey, near Norwich, works at Serco and appeared at Ipswich Magistrates' Court on Monday.

He was remanded in custody and will appear at Norwich Crown Court on 14 September.

The charge stated that between 3 and 14 August, while acting as a public officer employed by Serco, Jobson "wilfully and without reasonable excuse or justification" committed misconduct in a way which "amounted to an abuse of the public's trust in the office".

Norfolk Police said the charge was in connection to the "release of information relating to a number of addresses in Thetford, which were later targeted during several nights of violent disorder in the town".

A spokesperson for Serco said: "This matter is currently being handled by the police, and we are cooperating fully. As this relates to an ongoing legal process, it would be inappropriate to comment further."

News.title: PM says he's not embarrassed about hoax message exchange
News.content:
Andy Burnham says he is not embarrassed that he exchanged messages with a person posing as US President Donald Trump's chief of staff.

The prime minister added all politicians face "these challenges" but insisted he did "everything right" in how he handled the security breach.

News website Politico first reported, external that Burnham communicated with a person claiming to be Susie Wiles. Burnham said there was a "minimal exchange of information of zero consequence".

Liberal Democrat MP James MacCleary has written to Parliament's Intelligence and Security Committee (ISC) to ask them to consider investigating what he called an "egregious security breach".

It is understood the communication between Burnham and the person posing as Wiles was in the form of messages and there was no conversation between the two.

Asked if he was embarrassed about the incident, Burnham told broadcasters: "No, I am not because there was a minimal exchange, nothing of consequence and quickly I realised that this needed to be reported and I did so.

"So I handled it in the right way. All politicians are receiving these pressures and these challenges, but I did everything right."

Pressed on what action is being taken to find out who was behind the incident and to improve systems, Burnham said the "correct action" had been taken both in the UK and the US, without providing further details.

MacCleary, in his letter to ISC chairman Lord Beamish, said the security of the prime minister's communications "ought to be an absolute priority".

He added: "We need to understand how this breach could occur, or else risk it being repeated."

News.title: How soon will the drought be over?
News.content:
It is the question many people are asking: when will the drought be over, and how much rain will it take for things to return to normal?

Contrary to public perception, a drought does not end with a few days of rain.

Water must flow back into rivers, reservoirs, and the stores beneath our feet in the tiny spaces between soil, sand, and rock. This can take months.

According to scientists, the key question is not "Has it rained?" but "have water resources recovered?"

News.title: National Television Awards pick first all-female shortlist for drama acting award
News.content:
National Television Awards voters have selected an all-female shortlist in the best drama performance category for the first time.

The five nominees include previous winner Sheridan Smith, who played campaigner Ann Ming in ITV true crime drama I Fought The Law, and Gavin & Stacey's Ruth Jones for her role in Netflix thriller Run Away.

Vicky McClure gets the nod as Trigger Point's Lana Washington, while Ella Bruccoleri is shortlisted for alternative period drama The Other Bennet Sister, and Judy Parfitt is nominated for playing Sister Monica Joan in Call The Midwife.

The nominees were chosen in a public vote from an initial longlist that also included stars like David Tennant, Gary Oldman, Idris Elba, James Norton and Tom Hiddleston.

A second stage of voting is now open to pick the winners in the NTAs' 15 categories.

Elsewhere on this year's shortlists, Stacey Solomon has scored a hat-trick of nominations including best TV presenter.

That particular award was won last year by then-outgoing Match of the Day presenter Gary Lineker, breaking Ant and Dec's remarkable 23-year winning run.

Solomon will go up against the Geordie duo for this year's gong as well as Sir David Attenborough in his 100th birthday year, Traitors and chat show host Claudia Winkleman and Alison Hammond.

In the inaugural celebrity-led reality docuseries award, Solomon and her partner Joe Swash face competition from boxer Tyson Fury, Jeremy Clarkson and Emmerdale actor-turned-farmer Kelvin Fletcher, as well as funny fishermen Bob Mortimer and Paul Whitehouse.

Mrs Brown's Boys â which this week officially cancelled its festive specials due to creator and star Brendan O'Carroll's broken jaw - has a nomination for best comedy.

Other nominated shows include Canadian breakout romance Heated Rivalry (for best new drama) - eligible as it was co-produced by Sky - and Winkleman and Tess Daly's final series of Strictly Come Dancing (for best talent show).

The NTAs, which recognise the best in British TV over the past twelve months, first launched in 1995 and the winners will be voted for by the public between now and midday on 8 September - the day of the ceremony.

Hosted again by comedian Joel Dommett, the event will take place at London's O2 arena and will be broadcast live on ITV1 and ITVX from 20:00 BST.

News.title: Earl Spencer to publish story of his sister, Princess Diana
News.content:
Earl Spencer is to publish a new book telling the life story of his sister, Diana, Princess of Wales, from his perspective.

Swan Song: Diana, My Sister is due to be released in the UK next month, nearly 30 years after she died.

"I want to speak on Diana's behalf and do so in an openly positive way," Earl Spencer said of his reasons for writing the book.

He added that he hoped it would enable people to understand who she really was: "A one-off, dynamic character, full of love, charisma and self-doubt, who gave life a hell of a go, and left the world a far better place, despite exiting the stage while still so young."

Princess Diana, who died aged 36 following a car crash in Paris in 1997, would have turned 65 on 1 July this year.

Her sons Prince William and Prince Harry were aged 15 and 12 respectively at the time of her death.

In a statement released on Tuesday to mark the new book, Earl Spencer said he had been "inundated yet again" with requests for interviews about his sister, with the 30th anniversary of her death approaching.

"This has convinced me to write down my own thoughts and memories, once and for all, rather than having the discomfort of again reading the opinions of others, many of which are based on untruths that have become accepted over time," he said.

"The aim of this book is to tell the truth about Diana from her brother's perspective, just as I attempted to do when speaking at her funeral," he added, referring to the eulogy he delivered in Westminster Abbey in September 1997.

He said he hoped the book would be of interest to those who "still cherish" Diana's memory from when she was alive.

"And I would be delighted if those too young to remember her in her heyday feel - after reading this - that they 'get' who she really was," he continued.

In his eulogy, Earl Spencer described as Diana the "very essence of compassion, of duty, of style, of beauty", adding: "All over the world she was a symbol of selfless humanity... a standard bearer for the rights of the truly downtrodden."

He also used the speech to blame the media for her death, calling her the "most hunted person of the modern age" and pledged to protect Prince William and Prince Harry and prevent them suffering a similar fate.

The book is expected to be out on 22 September in the UK, and will be published by Penguin Michael Joseph, a division of Penguin Random House.

Daniel Bunyard, publishing director at Penguin Random House UK, said: "While these pages contain many revelations that will draw considerable attention, readers will find, for the first time, but also for all time, a fitting tribute to the beloved woman who was Princess Diana."

News.title: Officers told not to pursue car on wrong side of motorway before crash, says Ireland's police body
News.content:
GardaÃ­ (Irish police) were instructed to disengage from pursuing a car as it drove in the wrong direction on a motorway before a fatal crash, the Garda Representative Association has said.

Five teenagers were killed in the head-on crash on the M9 in County Kildare on Sunday morning.

Two women are in a critical condition, while another woman and a seven-year-old boy are in a serious condition.

Assistant General Secretary of the Garda Representative Association (GRA), Tara McManus, told the BBC that garda roads policing officers "do not have pursuit training".

She said officers involved in the Kildare incident were given a command to "disengage" with the car after it took "evasive action".

Ireland's Minister for Justice Jim O'Callaghan said that the Garda Commissioner has said he would introduce pursuit training this year.

The crash happened on the M9 Northbound at Junction 3 at about 03:00 local time.

The five teenagers who died have been named locally as Joe Carthy from Athy, County Kildare, Alex McCarthy from Carlow, Kamil Pustkowski from Limerick, Jeremy O'Brien and Jack Kennedy, according to Irish broadcaster RTÃ News.

The injured family - two women aged in their 30s and one in her 20s, and the young boy - are understood to be from Carlow.

McManus said the teenagers had been in the car for a number of hours before the collision and gardaÃ­ had attempted to interact with them and bring the vehicle to a stop on "several occasions".

She told BBC NI's Good Morning Ulster programme that officers deployed stinger devices in an attempt to stop the car, but it proceeded to travel in the direction of the motorway.

"At that stage our members would not continue in that pursuit and the directions that were given by our command and control centre were to disengage," she said.

"That would be the normal procedure for us that we do not engage with a car that has decided to take that sort of evasive action."

News.title: AI to help planes avoid climate-warming vapour trails
News.content:
We've all looked up and seen the white lines trailing behind aircraft in the sky.

Known as contrails, these icy clouds contribute to climate change, and scientists have been trying to work out how to stop them.

Now, a Â£5m UK trial will test whether AI can help, by predicting where warming contrails are likely to form and getting planes to avoid those areas.

It will focus on the Shanwick Oceanic airspace in the eastern half of the North Atlantic corridor which accounts for approximately 5% of global contrail warming.

The 30-month Operation Blue Skies project brings together Google, the UK government, the Met Office, air traffic control provider National Air Traffic Services (NATS) and researchers at the University of Cambridge and Imperial College London.

Contrails - also known as vapour trails - are made when the hot exhaust from aircraft engines meets the cold air at high altitude, creating ice crystals.

Many disappear quickly, but in particularly cold and humid conditions they can persist and spread, forming clouds which trap heat that would otherwise escape from the Earth.

Dr Paul Hodgson, Google's technical lead for the operation, told the BBC's Tech Life programme his five-year-old has a more colourful description for the white lines - "sky graffiti".

"We think that contrail warming is responsible for something like a third of all aviation climate warming," he said.

Dr Hodgson acknowledged there was uncertainty around the precise figure, but said scientists were confident it was "either quite a large problem or a very large problem".

The project also comes as the government backs expansion of UK airports, raising the wider question of whether tech solutions can sufficiently reduce aviation's environmental impact as demand for flying grows.

Google is also one of many big tech companies spending billions on new data centres - the giant, power-hungry banks of computer chips which power AI - which environmentalists are concerned will contribute even more to climate change.

News.title: Wetherspoons bans customers playing music from phones in pubs
News.content:
Wetherspoons has banned its customers from playing music out loud or taking calls on speaker, saying the noise from phones and tablets was an increasing problem driving people "nuts".

The company â which runs 792 pubs and bars across the UK â said that following complaints it has asked customers to switch their devices to silent or to use earphones.

Polling in recent years by various organisations suggests people are largely opposed to others playing music or taking calls on speaker in public spaces.

Wetherspoons told the BBC that staff would be asked to use "common sense" when enforcing the ban.

"We are not looking to ask anyone to leave a pub if they go against the ruling, but it is an option for managers if they refuse to do so," the company said.

The British Beer and Pub Association, which represents Wetherspoons and several other pub companies in the UK, said that "having a clear policy helps staff enforce rules and customers know what they can and can't do".

The group added: "We're yet to hear of anyone who relishes having a pint against the backdrop of a speakerphone call or someone loudly playing a video, so we expect this move will be greatly welcomed."

Studies suggest the majority of Britons are annoyed by hearing people take calls on speakerphone or playing videos or music on their phones without headphones.

A Transport for London survey of 1,000 people last year found 70% of respondents found loud music and phone calls without headphones a nuisance.

However, the evidence also suggests there is a clear generational gap. In an Ofcom survey of 1,010 people in August 2022, of the 13-to-17-year-olds questioned, 69% said it was acceptable to make video calls, 73% to listen to music and 83% to watch videos without headphones.

News.title: Ferguson shipyard to cut a quarter of its workforce
News.content:
Scotland's state-owned shipyard is to cut nearly a quarter of its total workforce while it waits for confirmation of promised new orders.

Workers at Ferguson Marine have been invited to apply for voluntary redundancy as construction draws to a close on the second of two long-delayed CalMac ferries.

The Port Glasgow firm currently employs 247 core staff, 31 agency staff and 32 apprentices - but says it expects to shed 70 posts through a voluntary redundancy process.

The Scottish government has promised to directly award the yard new orders for four smaller ships, but ministers say they are still conducting "due diligence" on the plan.

Ferguson Marine said the job losses would protect the long-term viability of the yard - but unions described the move as "a betrayal of a blameless workforce".

BBC Scotland News understands those who choose to leave the firm will receive Â£1,000 per completed year of service, up to Â£10,000, on top of their statutory entitlements.

News.title: One dead and hundreds ill in UK salmonella outbreak
News.content:
Symptoms include stomach cramps, diarrhoea, vomiting or fever. These usually develop between 12 and 72 hours after becoming infected.

Anyone who is concerned should contact their GP or out of hours service in the first instance, says the UKHSA.

Most cases - 199 of the 207 - have been in England, including 47 in London and 38 in Yorkshire and Humber.

Hannah Charles, lead epidemiologist for gastrointestinal infections at UKHSA, said: "We're working with Food Standards Agency and other public health agencies to investigate a salmonella outbreak that may be linked to eggs imported from outside of the UK."

Salmonella can be found in a number of food sources including raw or under-cooked poultry or meat and eggs.

Preparing and cooking food thoroughly can prevent infection, as well as washing your hands after using the bathroom and before handling food.

Thousands of cases food poisoning happen each year in the UK caused by lots of different strains of salmonella.

It is more unusual to see an outbreak like this linked to one specific strain of the bacterium affecting many people at one time.

The UKHSA says "extensive" epidemiological and food chain investigations are ongoing to identify the source but that egg consumption remains the strongest to date.

People appear to have fallen ill after eating out rather than after consuming food prepared at home.

Some of the food businesses linked to 24 of the cases use imported eggs.

"At this time there is no identified link to UK-produced eggs or poultry," says the UKHSA.

Any extra precautions or preventative measures will be implemented if needed, it says. The risk to the general public is low.

Jacquelyn McCormick, Head of Incidents at the Food Standards Agency, said eggs which are thoroughly cooked and handled hygienically should not present a food safety risk.

She advised: "Infants, young children, pregnant people and older adults should only eat runny or raw eggs if they have a British Lion mark or are produced under the Laid in Britain egg assurance scheme."

People handling eggs, eggshells or egg packaging should wash their hands thoroughly with soap and water, she added.

Catering outlets have a food hygiene rating, so looking at these when deciding where to eat, recommends Dr Kathleen O'Reilly from the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine.

News.title: Disabled people in England to get 24-hour free bus travel
News.content:
Disabled people in England will be able to travel by bus for free at any time of day from April, the government has announced.

Currently, disabled bus passes are only eligible for use between the hours of 09:30 and 23:00 on weekdays, making it difficult for people to get to work or attend later evening events. They can be used at any time of day at the weekend and on bank holidays.

It is believed about one million people could benefit from the change, which forms part of the government's focus on reducing the cost of living and encouraging people into work.

The disability charity Scope said the move would "remove barriers to everyday life".

According to the government, bus travel is the most popular mode of transport in England and a "lifeline for so many".

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said it was "simply not right that many disabled people cannot travel using their pass during certain times of the day".

He said the government would change that, as he had done previously in his role as mayor of Greater Manchester.

Earlier this year, Burnham removed time-restricted travel for those with disabled passes in Manchester so they could use the city's bus system, known as the Bee Network, at any time of day.

"I'm proud to do it now for the whole country," he added.

Tom Gordon, Liberal Democrat MP for Harrogate and Knaresborough and prominent advocate for the policy, called it a "huge win for the disabled community" and a "culmination of two years of campaigning".

But a Conservative Party spokesman asked the prime minister to "come clean" on how he was going to fund "this growing list of policies".

"This is simply the shuffling around of existing departmental budgets," they added.

News.title: Ex-workers tell of 'chaotic atmosphere' at new £400m prison
News.content:
The UK's newest prison has had a "chaotic atmosphere" in its first 18 months, former workers have told a BBC investigation.

HMP Millsike, in East Yorkshire, was heralded by the government for setting "the standard for the future" when it opened in March 2025 with 1,500 places.

But former workers have described under-staffing, inadequate training and seeing specialist officers called in to deal with serious incidents on numerous occasions.

Mitie, the company that runs the category C prison, said safety was its "highest priority" and it was "operating in line with plans agreed with the Ministry of Justice".

News.title: Gillian Anderson felt 'betrayed' by The Salt Path allegations after appearing in adaptation
News.content:
The Salt Path star Gillian Anderson has said allegations that the memoir was fabricated felt like "a betrayal" after spending time with the couple.

Anderson played Raynor Winn in the film adaptation of the 2018 memoir, which was released in the UK last year.

It tells the story of how Winn and her husband Moth, who was diagnosed with a neurological condition, walked the South West Coast Path after losing their Welsh home.

But an investigation by the Observer suggested some of Winn's claims about the events that had led to the couple losing their home had been misrepresented.

Winn previously described the Observer's article as "highly misleading" and said the couple had been taking legal advice.

The book and its film adaptation depict a couple who decide to walk the 630-mile (1,013km) route after their home was repossessed following a bad business deal.

But the Observer reported that Winn - whose legal name is Sally Walker - and her husband, Moth Winn, had lost their home after she had taken out a loan to repay money she had been accused of stealing from her previous employer, Martin Hemmings, an estate agent and property surveyor from north Wales.

In a statement issued last year, Winn said she stood by the book's description of how they came to lose their house, saying the dispute with the Hemmings did not result in her and her husband losing their home.

News.title: Heavy showers and thunderstorms bring risk of flash flooding to UK
News.content:
Wet weather is forecast for parts of the UK following a summer of record-breaking heatwaves and widespread drought.

Although heavy showers are expected for many, the places across England and Wales most in need of significant rain may not see much of it in the coming days.

Most of the showers will fall across parts of north-west England, Northern Ireland and southern Scotland, with some parts of south-east England staying dry.

Where the heaviest showers do fall, there is a risk of hail, lightning and the potential for flash flooding.

News.title: Water supply restored to 7,400 properties in Kent, South East Water says
News.content:
Drinking water supplies have been restored to about 7,600 properties in Kent which have been experiencing no water or low pressure, South East Water (SEW) has said.

More than 8,000 customers were affected by the latest supply disruptions, which SEW said was a result of prolonged hot weather, high demand, pipe bursts, and power issues.

The company said supplies had been restored to properties in Herne Bay, Rough Common and Blean, but urged all customers to use water for "essential" purposes only.

About 400 properties in Benenden, Cranbrook and Rolvenden are continuing to experience low pressure or no water and properties in Herne Bay might experience "intermittent supplies" later, SEW added.

Harry Kane is prepared to open discussions with Bayern Munich over a contract extension with the reigning Bundesliga champions.

The England captain has entered the final 12 months of the original four-year agreement he signed after transferring from Tottenham Hotspur for £86.4 million back in August 2023.

In a video broadcast by Kicker, Kane said: "We obviously said we wanted to talk after the World Cup and after my holiday. So I’m not sure exactly when, but they’ll start this week, next week… we’ll start those talks.

"Like I’ve said before, we’re calm, I think they’re calm with the situation.

"Obviously now is the time to start talking, because there’s only a year left. That’s important. But both sides are relaxed, and I’m pretty sure there’ll be some talks this week or next week."

open image in gallery Harry Kane is set to open contract talks with Bayern Munich ( PA Wire )

The 33-year-old striker, who rejoined Bayern’s squad prior to Saturday’s Supercup clash against Borussia Dortmund, also assessed his Ballon d’Or prospects while insisting that the honour is not at the front of his thoughts.

"The Ballon d’Or is as big as it gets, from an individual point of view," he said. "I know I had a great season last season, but the focus is on this new season."

During this summer's tournament in North America, Kane became England’s leading World Cup scorer, reaching 14 goals in 18 appearances to surpass Gary Lineker’s record of 10.

However, he was unable to lead England to World Cup glory as the Three Lions crashed out in the semi-finals following defeat by Argenitna.

But Kane did score 61 goals in 51 outings across all competitions for Bayern last season, securing the Bundesliga top scorer award for the third consecutive year.

"The Ballon d’Or’s not in my hands," he continued. "I’ve done what I can do in terms of putting in the performances. It’s now down to votes and other people and the media – stuff I can’t control – so we’ll see what happens.

"Obviously, it would be amazing if it was to happen. But ultimately, it’s still two or three months away before that’s decided so it’s not something that’s at the front of my mind right now."

The Trump White House staffer once labeled as the president’s “human printer” now has a new nickname after she was revealed to be one of the few aides chosen to accompany him during his clandestine escape from Air Force One in Turkey after this year’s NATO summit last month.

According to New York Times reporter Maggie Haberman, the president chose executive assistant Natalie Harp to be among the trio who joined him in an airline catering truck to secretly transfer from the Air Force One Boeing 747 to a smaller plane for a flight from Ankara to RAF Mildenhall because she serves as a living security blanket for the 80-year-old chief executive.

"Natalie Harp, because she is sort of his Binkie, for lack of a better way of putting it — his comfort blanket,” Haberman said during an appearance on MSNOW Sunday while explaining his choices to host Jacob Soboroff.

Haberman similarly said Trump chose the other two aides who joined him — Walt Nauta and Dan Scavino — because of their long tenure serving him in sensitive roles, with Scavino’s employment dating back decades to his days as a teenage golf caddy at one of Trump’s golf clubs.

Nauta, whose title is director of Oval Office Operations, was once Trump’s military valet during his first term but followed him into political exile in Florida after he lost the 2020 election, later becoming a co-defendant in the case brought against Trump for allegedly illegally retaining classified documents at his Florida home after the end of his first term.

open image in gallery Trump's executive assistant, Natalie Harp, is seen disembarking from Marine One after landing in Washington on Sunday ( Getty )

open image in gallery Natalie Harp, an aide to President Trump, was one of just a small handful of aides who accompanied him as he left Air Force One behind as a decoy amid an Iranian threat while traveling from Turkey ( Getty )

According to Haberman, the former Navy Chief Petty Officer still functions like a body man and is always carrying a brown briefcase that accompanies the president — containing hair spray, breath mints and “all kinds of stuff."

But Trump’s relationship with Harp has taken on more and more scrutiny from the public in the days since his secret plane switch became public.

The 34-year-old had in the past attracted concerns from the Secret Service and others in his orbit for leaving notes declaring her admiration for the 80-year-old former reality TV host.

Harp’s brother, from whom she is estranged, has called her relationship with the president “unhealthy” and referred to her as Trump’s “fan club.”

open image in gallery New York Times reporter Maggie Haberman (pictured in the White House briefing room last year) has a new nickname for Trump’s close personal aide Natalie Harp ( Getty )

She earned her “human printer” nickname because she regularly provides Trump with large-format printouts of news articles and social media posts, even his own.

But in recent years Harp has taken on yet another critical role in Trump’s orbit — authoring the Truth Social posts he often dictates.

A video from the Apple TV documentary The Art of the Surge shows Harp taking on that task that was previously performed by Scavino, while Trump and his top aides watched then-vice president Kamala Harris’ 2024 convention speech.

The Independent reported in February that Harp, a former right-wing television personality, has long been one of the people with access to Trump’s Truth Social account and was responsible for posting a racist video which depicted former president Barack Obama and his wife Michelle as apes.

Harp, who sits just outside the Oval Office during her work days, manages the president’s day to day social media posting — when he is not doing so himself.

Natalie Harp, one of President Donald Trump’s closest aides, is reportedly leaning into her nickname “the human printer” by passing along messages to the president the best way she knows how: printing them out.

Harp, 35, is known to carry a portable printer to present physical copies of supportive social media posts or op-eds for Trump to review, because it’s the president’s preferred method of digesting content.

But she also does the same for messages, according to a Politico article.

One person who wanted to give a physical message to Trump told Politico they texted the material to Harp, who replied, “printed.”

The one-word response is apparently the closest someone can get to a read receipt from the president.

open image in gallery Natalie Harp is one of President Trump’s most devoted aides and is constantly seen at his side, providing him with physical copies of flattering op-eds or social media posts to keep his spirits high ( AFP/Getty )

The Independent has asked the White House for comment.

Harp has been a loyal aide to Trump for many years. She’s consistently photographed at the president’s side or, at least, nearby – sometimes holding a stack of papers for Trump to review.

One of her main duties is to provide Trump with a stream of positive news, op-eds and social media commentary while also showing him criticisms of his opponents. After compiling the content, she prints it out for the president to physically see.

Some of that content, once physically approved by the president, ends up on his Truth Social account, the Wall Street Journal reported.

But Harp also serves as the go-between for the president and allies, facilitating messages for Trump to see and respond to.

open image in gallery Harp’s nickname ‘the human printer’ stems from her job to print out physical copies of social media posts, articles, op-eds and messages for President Trump to review. One New York Times report alleged Harp carried a portable printer around to do so at any given time ( Reuters )

By establishing herself as the source of Trump’s positive feedback and casual communications, Harp has cemented herself as a crucial part of the Trump team in the White House. She’s so devoted to the president that she’s written heartfelt letters saying “You are all that matters to me,” the New York Times reported.

Trump seemingly returns the feelings, treating Harp as a “Binkie” or “his comfort blanket,” New York Times reporter Maggie Haberman described on MSNOW.

Harp’s unwavering allegiance to Trump has sparked speculation about the two’s close-knit relationship.

Harp’s brother, Preston Harp, described the relationship between the president and his sister as “very unhealthy” in an interview with The Daily Mail.

open image in gallery Harp is consistently at the president’s side and has been for many years, cementing her place in Trump’s inner circle ( AFP/Getty )

Preston Harp later told The Daily Beast that he believes his sister sees Trump “as a kind of father figure because he embodies the doctrine of American exceptionalism.”

This past month, Harp was among the few aides that Trump took with him on a military jet when he discreetly changed planes while flying out of Turkey due to security concerns.

Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff used the report to criticize the president, claiming he would rather “travel with Natalie on their apparently defenseless flying palace” than do his job.

TV presenter Richard Madeley has said he nearly choked to death on a piece of “very rare beef” before being saved by his sister.

The 70-year-old said he swallowed the food without chewing properly during a “lively discussion”.

The star said the piece of beef went “straight into the windpipe”.

Speaking on ITV’s Good Morning Britain to Dr Hilary Jones, Madeley said: “I tried to cough it up but I had no air in the lungs to do that. I suddenly realised I was choking.

“Pandemonium ensued. People came round behind me, they were hammering on my back. The minutes ticked by and it wouldn’t dislodge.

“After two-and-a-half, three minutes, I began to feel my world closing in, black dots coming on the side [of my eyes], I began to feel very weak and a calm sense of acceptance coming, ‘oh, this is it, this is how I’m going to go.’”

open image in gallery TV presenter Richard Madeley has said he nearly choked to death on a piece of ‘very rare beef’ ( Getty )

Liz Lawrence, Madeley’s sister who is trained in performing the Heimlich manoeuvre, was present at the dinner and rushed in from the toilet to save him.

Madeley said: “She did the Heimlich on me. One, two, three times and it didn’t work, it was still lodged.

“I felt my knees give way and I went down and as I went down, thank God, she did it again.

“The combination of gravity and her doing it harder than ever before dislodged the beef, got a little bit of air in and managed to cough it up, and 10 seconds later I was back in the room, but it was touch and go.

“If she hadn’t known what to do, I would’ve died.”

According to the North West Ambulance Service, there are a number of steps you can take should you think someone is choking.

open image in gallery If the person becomes unresponsive, an emergency 999 call should be made immediately ( Getty/iStock )

The service advises members of the public to encourage the person choking “to cough to try to clear the blockage”, before leaning them forward and placing “five sharp blows between their shoulder blades with the heel of your hand”, should coughing not prove effective.

Should this still not work, it says to “clench one fist and place it just above their belly button, place your other hand on top of your fist and pull sharply inwards and upwards”. This should be repeated up to five times.

If the person becomes unresponsive, an emergency 999 call should be made immediately.

News.title: Mamdani releases blooper reel after accusations his foreign language video was AI

News.content:

Georgia Hunter Bell nonchalantly raised her arms to the delight of a euphoric Birmingham home crowd after a supreme display to win a first European 1500m crown. Three-and-a-half laps of sheer dominance underlined a rare treble following victories at the World Indoor Championships and Commonwealth Games.

But despite immense success in 2026, the Olympic and World medallist quickly allowed her mind to drift before exiting the Alexander Stadium. Her curiosity and appetite for more, even “a bit of fomo”, left her imagining what role she might have played in the titanic 800m clash before, as European champion Audrey Werro took down Hunter Bell’s teammate Keely Hodgkinson and Femke Broeders-Bol.

Well, we will soon gain some insight, after it was confirmed that Hunter Bell will join that star-studded trio and World champion Lilian Odira in the Zurich Diamond League 800m next Thursday, in what could whet the appetite for a golden era in the event in the build-up to LA28.

“It was really close between me and Werro last year in Zurich,” Hunter Bell tells the Independent when looking ahead to the closing stages of her season. “It was a dip on the line, but this year is such a good lineup. It’s me, Keely, Werro, Femke and Lilian. I think it will be a really great race.

“I’m going to see about the Diamond League Final, too. I want to do it, but I also need to be conscious of how much racing I’m doing and training I’m missing. Then I need to make a decision about the World Ultimate Championships. I’ll definitely be doing it, but I haven’t decided which event right now.

“I do just feel like I really want an opportunity this year to be part of the big five, I guess, in the 800m. So that kind of opportunity with World Ultimate Championships, I think it would suit me quite well because there’ll be no pacemaker. There’ll be two rounds, so the endurance comes in a little bit more versus a one-off Diamond League, so I am kind of eyeing that up.”

It has been a lingering problem for Hunter Bell and coaches Trevor Painter and Jenny Meadows. A good problem, of course, with their athlete proving adept at both events: a 1500m bronze at the Paris Olympics and an 800m silver at the Tokyo World Championships last year, where she managed to edge out Hodgkinson behind Odira.

The potential is clearly there for an audacious attempt at a medal in both events, following in the footsteps of the legendary Kelly Holmes at the Athens Games in 2004, with the Beijing World Championships next year and the Los Angeles Olympics both proving enticing.

“Next year will be more of a year for taking that risk,” Hunter Bell adds. “I wanted to prove to everyone that I can win global titles across both events. I really want to try and do the double, probably at the Worlds in Beijing, but I am waiting to see that schedule.

“It will mean that I will be a lot more intentional with my races because I do usually race a lot. This year was going to be a lighter racing year, but I still think it’s going to end up around like 25 races. The last two years, I’ve done over 50 races.

open image in gallery Hunter Bell plans to join the star-studded ‘big five’ of teammate Hodgkinson, Audrey Werro, Femke Broeders-Bol and world champion Lilian Odira ( Reuters )

“To do the double, I would need to do everything right in training and then also be under-raced going into that. That is a big goal for me next year. I want to try that, and then depending on how that goes, [that] will impact whether I do it at the Olympics the following year.

“I think the races would be fine, but it’s really difficult to sleep after a race; your body is obviously really sore. So we need to practise working out how I can get to sleep no matter what and recover.

“I don’t just want to participate in both. If I’m going to do it, I want to at least medal in both.”

Part of Hunter Bell’s endurance is built on a fondness for the bike, with long rides factored into her training across camps in South Africa and Switzerland, both for the physical and mental benefits.

“It’s just so much fun. It’s like therapy,” Hunter Bell, who is also a Canyon athlete, adds. “It’s the one time of the week I find that I’m not really on my phone or, you know, not distracted by anything else. I am truly just looking around at my surroundings. It’s sociable too.

“I’ve been following the Tour de France all summer, too, and Demi [Vollering] is definitely someone that I really look up to. But you know, also Kasia [Niewiadoma-Phinney] the other day on Mont Ventoux. I’ve done that climb, and I know how hard it is. So it makes you have even more respect for how quickly they’re doing it.

open image in gallery Hunter Bell incorporates long cycle rides into her training ( PA Archive )

“My hope is next year to go to one of the classics, like Milan–San Remo or Paris–Roubaix and experience it with Canyon from [inside the support] car as well.”

Until then, there is more business on the track, with the M11 group back in training ahead of the Diamond League final. Hunter Bell and Hodgkinson are primed to join each other on the start line after sickness scuppered a showdown in London earlier this summer.

And despite a clinic from the outside of lane one in the 1500m on Sunday, it is the 800m that has lit a fire inside Hunter Bell to finish the season strongly, starting with those last punishing sessions alongside Hodgkinson.

“Of course we’re competitive, but it’s in a way that we’re not tearing the other one down,” Hunter Bell concludes. “It literally is just like us being competitive, and so we’re getting quicker.

“I just think the 800m is so fun right now because it’s not a sure thing of who’s going to win. And like me as a spectator, I’d be watching. Of course, you get nerves. But this is going to be really fun, so I think it’s great for the sport.”

Madonna has earned the highest number of nominations for the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards, the network announced on Tuesday.

Her recognition spans every decade of her musical career. To date, she holds 19 competitive VMA trophies and was recognized in 1986 as the inaugural solo female recipient of the Video Vanguard Award.

For the upcoming ceremony, she is nominated in 11 categories: video, artist, and song of the year, alongside best collaboration, dance, direction, art direction, cinematography, editing, choreography, and visual effects.

open image in gallery For the upcoming ceremony, she is nominated in 11 categories ( Warner Music )

Winning all 11 nominations would place her in a tie with Beyoncé and Taylor Swift as the most-honored musicians in the history of the VMAs, with 30 awards each. Eminem currently leads male artists with 15 wins.

Swift holds the second-highest tally this year with nine nods. A single victory at the event would secure her place as the most decorated artist in VMA history.

Her nominations cover video of the year, artist of the year, best pop, direction, art direction, cinematography, editing, choreography, and visual effects.

Ariana Grande and Sabrina Carpenter each secured seven nominations, while Bruno Mars, PinkPantheress, and Zara Larsson received five apiece. LISA of Blackpink picked up four nominations, while Shakira, Tate McRae, GENER8ION, and Yung Lean each received three.

The nominees competing alongside Madonna and Swift for artist of the year include Grande, Mars, Carpenter, and Morgan Wallen.

Contenders for the headline award, video of the year, are Swift’s "The Fate of Ophelia," Madonna’s "Confessions II — The Film," Grande’s "Hate That I Made You Love Me," Mars’ "I Just Might," Carpenter’s "Tear," and GENER8ION’s "Storm" featuring Yung Lean.

The two-hour presentation will air live from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on CBS at 7::green-background[30] p.m. Eastern and 4::green-background[30] p.m. Pacific on Sunday, Sept. 27. Viewers in the U.S. can also watch via an MTV simulcast or stream it on Paramount+.

International streaming access via Paramount+ and MTV will follow the next day.

CBS broadcasts several major ceremonies, such as the Tony Awards and the American Music Awards. The network has carried the Grammy Awards since 1973, though broadcasting rights will move to ABC starting in 2027.

A total of 26 artists received their first VMA nominations this year. Among them are GENER8ION and Yung Lean—who earned three nominations for their joint track "Storm"—as well as K-pop group CORTIS and viral singer Stella Lefty, known for "Boston," with two nods each. Additional first-time nominees comprise Don Toliver, Kali Uchis, Noah Kahan, Olivia Dean, Tucker Wetmore, and Sienna Spiro.

Reintroduced after a seven-year absence, the best dance category features McRae’s "Nobody’s Girl," Bebe Rexha and Faithless’ "New Religion," Harry Styles’ "Aperture," Lady Gaga and Doechii’s "Runaway," Madonna’s "Confessions II — The Film," PinkPantheress’ "Stateside" featuring Larsson, and Slayyyter’s "Dance …"

Public voting opened online Tuesday for 13 categories, with polls closing on Sept. 25 at 6 p.m. Eastern and 3 p.m. Pacific.

Voting for best new artist will continue throughout the live broadcast.

News.title: Unemployment rate fails to fall for Burnham
News.content:
An expected drop in the unemployment rate has failed to materialise, dealing a setback to Andy Burnham’s hopes of reviving Britain’s ailing economy.

Unemployment remained stuck at 4.9pc in the three months to June, while the number of payrolled employees fell by 13,000, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics. Economists had predicted that the unemployment rate would ease to 4.8pc.

While the three-month figure was flat, monthly data showed a sharp increase at the end of the period. Unemployment jumped to 5.4pc in June, up from 4.6pc the previous month.

That marked the highest reading since October 2020 and the biggest monthly jump in 13 years.

Julian Jessop, at the Institute of Economic Affairs, described the latest jobs figures as “dire”.

He said: “The unemployment rate remains stubbornly high, with a big jump in the single month figure for June.”

It came as private sector wage growth slumped to a six-year low of just 2.8pc. That stands in contrast to a 6.1pc pay increase for the average public sector worker in the same period.

Meanwhile, vacancies dropped to 707,000 in the three months to July – the lowest level since 2021 – with a particular strain on entry-level job openings.

Ben Harrison, director of the Work Foundation at Lancaster University, warned that the UK was “trapped in a deepening jobs drought”.

Thomas Pugh, chief economist at RSM UK, said: “Stagnant, or even negative, real wage growth in the second half of this year will intensify the pressure on Burnham and Healey to come up with a package to support the cost of living.

“However, doing anything substantial without breaching either the fiscal rules or the manifesto commitments looks increasingly difficult given the deterioration in headroom and commitments to spend big on everything from defence to social care.”

News.title: Top British scientist steps down from WHO
News.content:
One of Britain’s best-known scientists has resigned as assistant director-general of the World Health Organization.

Sir Jeremy Farrar became a household name during the pandemic when he served on the UK’s Scientific Advisory Group for Emergencies (Sage).

Sources inside the WHO and the broader scientific community told The Telegraph he resigned his position on Monday.

While it is not clear what prompted his resignation, colleagues told The Telegraph he had been unhappy within the organisation for some time. One speculated that he had become increasingly frustrated with its internal politics and bureaucracy.

Sir Jeremy, 64, who was also a former director of the Wellcome Trust, could not immediately be reached for comment.

The surprise move comes at a difficult time for the WHO, which is undergoing a major restructuring after suffering cuts and a massive funding shortfall following the United States’s withdrawal from it in January. It is also fighting a major outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the WHO’s Director-General, announced Dr Farrar’s decision in an email to all staff on Tuesday morning, saying that the British scientist will “retire” from the WHO, effective September 30.

In the email, seen by The Telegraph, Dr Tedros said: “Dr Farrar has demonstrated an exceptional commitment to science and public health at the highest levels, and we are grateful that he chose to bring his experience, energy and conviction to WHO.

“On behalf of the entire organisation, I extend my sincere thanks to Dr Farrar... [and wish] him every success in his next chapter and a well-deserved retirement.”

He added that Dr Bruce Aylward will take over as the new Assistant Director-General for Health Promotion, Disease Prevention and Care.
